Commissioner Bethell appointed to national youth housing and homelessness task force
Commissioner Danielle Bethell has been named to a national task force focused on youth housing and homelessness. The group will examine ways counties can support young people experiencing housing instability across the country.
Commissioner Danielle Bethell was appointed to the National Association of Counties Youth Housing and Homelessness Task Force, according to a Sep. 30 announcement. She is one of 22 county officials nationwide selected to address how counties can better support young people facing homelessness and housing instability.
"I'm incredibly honored to be selected to be a part of this work," said Commissioner Bethell. “I look forward to working with county leaders from across the country, sharing about Marion County and Oregon, and bringing back ideas that will help us reach our local youth facing housing challenges."
More than 4.2 million youth and young adults experience homelessness in the United States each year. The task force operates as part of NACo’s Building Better Futures initiative.
"During my decades of public service, I have seen firsthand the multifaceted, evolving challenges facing our youth," said NACo President George Dunlap. "Through this task force, we will have a unique chance to diagnose emerging concerns and align proven strategies, especially as it pertains to addressing youth housing instability and homelessness."
The group will meet from October 2026 through July 2027, concluding its work at the 2027 NACo Annual Conference.
Marion County covers approximately 1,182 square miles in Oregon’s Willamette Valley region and serves more than 348,000 residents across 20 incorporated cities as well as unincorporated communities; it operates as a full-service local government focused on public safety, health services, transportation infrastructure, cultural preservation—including historic landmarks such as the Oregon State Capitol—and community support initiatives led by its Board of Commissioners, who provide leadership on policy issues while ensuring fiscal accountability and empowerment for residents, according to the official website.
